chapter: Setting the record straight on Hendersonia
title: Disputing Hendersonia claims about Baron Lee and Jimmy Murray bands
summary: Horace rejects that Fletcher fronted Baron Lee's band in 1936 or took over Jimmy Murray's band in 1942, since the brothers both had to be at the Grand Terrace.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Here's another one, "February, 1936, he fronted the Baron Lee Band for a short tour of New England, while Horace directed his own band at the Grand Terrace. Now again, I don't know --

He always was at the Grand Terrace for a number of reasons. He was broadcasting from the Grand Terrace, plus the fact that one of us had to either play piano or the other directed the show, or either I had to direct the show and he'd play the piano on certain things. So both of us were essential to be there, so Fletcher never did that. So where that information came about, I would like to challenge that.

Okay. Here's another one -- "March 1942" -- clear up in the '40's -- "he took over the Jimmy Murray Band from Pittsburgh and played dates in Albany and Washington. He had fired his 802 band, but there seems to be a period of overlap when the latter" -- meaning the 802 band -- "played Baltimore, probably under Horace's direction."
I don't know. Where does this information come from?
I'm very happy to hear this. I am very happy to hear this. This I'm going to challenge.
